column1: She {{c1::has been working}} here since 2019 — and she still loves it.
column3: since + past starting point → present perfect; continuous for ongoing activity

column1: By the time the recruiter called back, I {{c1::had accepted}} another offer.
column3: by the time + past → the earlier event takes the past perfect

column1: When the assistant finally arrived, Marta {{c1::had been running}} the office alone for a year.
column3: duration up to a past moment → past perfect continuous

column1: As a trainee, he {{c1::used to know}} nothing about tax law.
column3: states take used to, never would

column1: Every Friday she {{c1::would stay}} late to plan the week ahead.
column3: would + infinitive → repeated past actions with a nostalgic colouring

column1: This time next week I {{c1::will be presenting}} to the board.
column3: future continuous → activity in progress at a future moment

column1: By May she {{c1::will have been leading}} the team for a decade.
column3: future perfect continuous → duration measured at a future point

column1: The CEO {{c1::is to step}} down at June's annual meeting.
column3: be to + infinitive → official arrangements, the press-release future

column1: I {{c1::was about to leave}} when the phone rang.
column3: be about to in the past → imminent action interrupted

column1: He {{c1::was to have taken}} over in May, but the merger collapsed.
column3: was to have done → a plan that never happened; the perfect marks non-fulfilment
